frames.narration: At 12:02 a customer orders two dishes for 24.50. The order API passes the request to the order service, which checks both items against the current menu, copies their names and prices into the order and authorises the card without taking the money yet. The order is in the state placed, version 1.

The order service writes the new state and an outbox record in one database transaction, so a change and its event cannot be separated. A relay then publishes the event on the bus. Everyone who needs to react learns about the order from there.

The restaurant tablet shows the order at once. At 12:03 the cook taps accept, and the request says it expects version 1. The state moves to accepted, version 2, and the kitchen starts preparing it (version 3). Based on this restaurant's open orders it expects the food to be ready at 12:14, 11 minutes from now.

At the very same moment the customer changes their mind and taps cancel, which also expects version 1. The order is already at version 3, so the database refuses the change. The customer sees that the kitchen has started and cannot cancel for free, and nothing is left half-done.

The dispatcher sees the accepted event and keeps the order until it is due: the food is ready at 12:14 and the nearest suitable courier is 7 minutes away, so the order becomes due around 12:07. At the 12:06 window it decides three due orders and four couriers together, and the best total cost gives this order to courier c-19, who will arrive just as the food does.

The ETA service adds the parts: pickup at 12:14, a 14 minute trip to the customer and 4 minutes to park and hand over. It tells the customer to expect the food at about 12:32, with a range of 12:29 to 12:36, and it will recompute the number whenever the kitchen or the courier changes.

The courier reaches the restaurant at 12:14, as the food comes off the pass, so the food waits 0 minutes. The courier taps picked up, expecting version 3, and the order moves to version 4. The customer's app switches to live tracking.

The courier arrives at 12:31, a minute ahead of the estimate, and taps delivered. A weak signal makes the app send the tap twice with the same request id. The first moves the order to delivered, version 5, and the card is charged. The second is recognised and ignored, so there is one charge and one payout. The order took 29 minutes.
